rules.message: Supabase query using service role key — bypasses Row Level Security
rules.detail: The service role key bypasses all RLS policies. Never use it in client-side code or expose it to users. Use the anon key with proper RLS policies for client operations, and the service role only in trusted server-side code.

rules.message: Supabase client created without auth context in server-side code
rules.detail: Creating a Supabase client with just the anon key in server code does not apply the authenticated user's RLS policies. Use createServerClient with the user's session cookie to inherit their permissions.

rules.message: Supabase rpc() or raw SQL built from user input
rules.detail: Building SQL strings for Supabase rpc() calls or using .select() with template literals containing user input allows SQL injection. Use parameterised rpc() arguments or Supabase's query builder methods.

rules.message: Supabase table query without filtering by authenticated user
rules.detail: Querying Supabase tables without filtering by the authenticated user's ID can expose data belonging to other users if RLS is not enabled on the table. Always add .eq('user_id', session.user.id) or rely on RLS policies.

rules.message: Supabase Storage bucket created with public access
rules.detail: Creating a public storage bucket makes all files accessible to anyone with the URL. Use private buckets and signed URLs for sensitive files.

rules.message: Supabase upsert() with unvalidated request body
rules.detail: Spreading the full request body into upsert() allows users to set fields they shouldn't control (e.g. role, is_admin). Validate and allowlist fields before upserting.

cves.description: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Attributes

rules.message: Supabase auth.admin used — ensure this is server-side only
rules.detail: supabase.auth.admin methods use the service role and bypass security. If this code runs on the client side or is reachable by users, it creates a critical privilege escalation vulnerability.
